requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: firewalld was active and enabled, runtime and permanent rules agreed, and after a node1 reboot with a changed boot identity the service and rules recovered unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Allow SSH to node1 from any address.
requirements.summary: The public-zone SSH service remained enabled, sshd listened on all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and node2 and node3 reached TCP/22 before and after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow TCP port 9000 only from node2 and reject node3 and all other sources.
requirements.summary: A higher-priority IPv4 accept rule was limited to node2's 10.100.1.11/32 address, followed by blanket IPv4 and IPv6 reject rules. With a bounded listener running, node2 received HTTP 200 while node3 was rejected immediately; the same behavior was demonstrated after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6 before and after execution. The existing firewalld installation was used, with package health remaining clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct configuration and behavior checks show persistent firewalld rules, unrestricted SSH, node2-only access to TCP/9000, rejection of node3 and other IPv4/IPv6 sources, and preservation of AlmaLinux 9.6 and its kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol was completed coherently on all three nodes: each had a healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered services/network behavior, corroborated by the lifecycle boot snapshots.
limitations: Only node2 and node3 were used as live remote TCP/9000 clients; rejection of every other IPv4 source and all IPv6 sources is supported by the blanket firewall rules rather than exhaustive behavioral probes.

The nodes expose no distinct application data store or cluster subsystem, so restart recovery evidence covers system health, networking, services, firewall state, and the scoped access path rather than separate data or cluster-state checks.
The lifecycle collector does not inventory firewall rules, so final firewall state relies on the executor's direct runtime and permanent firewalld observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing actions had clear roles: persistent rule configuration, a bounded TCP/9000 test listener, required restart evidence, and listener cleanup. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutation was identified, and the listener plus its PID/log files were removed. The only hygiene defect is that each necessary reboot command left /tmp/reboot-request.log behind rather than cleaning it up; these small residual files remained on node1, node2, and node3. No failed services, damaged package state, or unexpected listening socket remained.
